title: 1000 People Died on This Boat in 20 Minutes
description:
June 1904. A church on New York's Lower East Side chartered the steamboat General Slocum for its annual picnic. Twenty minutes up the East River, fire started in a storage room full of lamp oil.

The captain went past the shore and ran a mile upriver instead, which drove the fire back into the passengers. The hoses burst. The lifeboats were wired down and painted to the deck. The cork in the life preservers had rotted, and the manufacturer had put bar iron inside them to meet the legal weight.

1,021 died, around 300 of them children. Seven men were indicted. Six were acquitted.
